### Contributing guidelines

- [X] I have read [CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md](https://github.com/nvim-mini/mini.nvim/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md)

### Module(s)

mini.ai, mini.surround

### Question

One problem I'm regularly running into while maintaining bash scripts is a quick keystroke to surround a bash variable use in quotes.   I have a neovim configuration mostly built around the mini modules so I'd be happy to add this config in the most mini-way possible. 

I think what I need to do is write a mini.ai custom_textobject pattern that matches `$VAR` or `${VAR}`?  from searching the treesitter docs I don't believe that is a pre-existing textobject defined by treesitter?

Has anyone done this before, or is there a simpler solution that I'm not seeing?

Apologies if this is the wrong forum for a question like this, but I'm struggling to put together the pieces to solve this problem.

comment_data.body:
> One problem I'm regularly running into while maintaining bash scripts is a quick keystroke to surround a bash variable use in quotes.
> ...
> I think what I need to do is write a mini.ai custom_textobject pattern that matches `$VAR` or `${VAR}`?

This indeed sounds like a correct direction: 1) create a custom 'mini.ai' textobject, like with `v` (variable) identifier; 2) use 'mini.surround' `add` mapping to surround the whole variable.

Here is how to create a custom 'mini.ai' textobject that would be active only in files with `sh` filetype (which bash scripts mostly are):
- Create a file `~/.config/after/ftplugin/sh.lua`. This is a filetype plugin for for `sh` filetype. I'd also probably recommend copying the future contents of this file to `~/.config/after/ftplugin/bash.lua`.
- Add the following lines to it:

    ```lua
    vim.b.miniai_config = {
      custom_textobjects = {
        -- Bash variable: $VAR, ${VAR}, $_VAR, $var, $_var123, etc.
        -- See `:h MiniAi-textobject-specification` for more details.
        v = { { '%$()[%a_][%w_]*()', '%${()[%a_][%w_]*()}' } },
      },
    }
    ```

Now opening the file with `sh` filetype (not necessarily the one that has `*.sh` extension, but the one which has `:=vim.bo.filetype` print `sh`) will have `av` select the whole variable (with `$` and `{}`) and `iv` select the variable name.

Surrounding now is done by the following sequence: `sa` (surround add) - `av` (around variable) - `"` (double quote). If you want this to be something faster (although I'd recommend sticking to this type of explicit surrounding), you can create a buffer-local keymap by adding the following call to the filetype plugin(s):

```lua
vim.keymap.set('n', '<Leader>v', 'saav"', { buf = 0, remap = true })
```

Hope this helps!

---
